verdict:
REJECT — RP_TAINTED, SIZE ZERO, and explicitly NOT OWNABLE AT ANY DISCOUNT while the litigation is live (blue SUSTAINED red 9/10, two findings reduced, none overturned; the winning ground moves).

WHAT DISQUALIFIES IT is a stack red under-weighted: an income incentive fee with NO TOTAL-RETURN REQUIREMENT paid to an adviser that is ALSO THE VALUATION DESIGNEE — the entity setting the marks is paid on the income those marks support; a LIVE §36(b) action (7:26-cv-03468) pleading exactly that conflict, WHICH THE 10-Q'S LITIGATION NOTE DOES NOT MENTION; and a dividend cut made INTO uncovered earnings with a $0.02 formulaic supplemental inflating the quoted yield. Per the RP_TAINTED gate, flagged names never qualify RP_FAIR, so the fairly-paid-risk route is closed regardless of price. Reopen needs ALL THREE: dismissal of the §36(b) action ON THE MERITS, discount >30% at NAV >=$14, and ex-largest-name implied mark below 35c for two consecutive quarters.

DOCTRINE CORRECTION APPLIED AT ADJUDICATION: blue also cited 'no edge: 14 analysts, consensus Buy, index membership'. Under §DIVERGENCE-NOT-COVERAGE (wired 2026-08-17) a coverage count is NOT a valid kill — it says the name is MEASURED, not measured correctly. That leg is VOID. The verdict stands entirely on the integrity stack, which is a data/integrity finding and kills under the response taxonomy on its own. Blue's adjacent point — zero capacity ceiling, 'the exact inverse of THE OFFICE THESIS' — IS valid, because it is about our structural edge rather than about how many analysts publish.

THE REUSABLE PRE-FLIGHT, and it is the best thing this court produced: READ THE LITIGATION NOTE BEFORE CREDITING A FILER WITH HONESTY. A live §36(b) action absent from the 10-Q's own litigation note is a disclosure finding available for the price of one fetch.
reopen_gates: NONE, SIZE ZERO, not ownable at any discount while 7:26-cv-03468 is live. Reopen requires ALL THREE: (a) dismissal of the §36(b) action ON THE MERITS, (b) discount >30% at NAV >=$14, (c) ex-largest-name implied mark below 35c for two consecutive quarters.
adjudicator_note: Same-adviser natural experiment (OTF vs OBDC, identical fee template). It did NOT expose mark posture as I predicted — marks were identical to the basis point across 115 shared tranches. It exposed ROE (OTF) and a fee/valuation-designee conflict (OBDC). The coverage-count leg of OBDC's kill is VOID under §DIVERGENCE-NOT-COVERAGE; the integrity stack carries it alone.
METRIC_INVALIDATION_20260818: *** METRIC INVALIDATED 2026-08-18 (OBDC blue bench) — READ BEFORE USING ANY 'IMPLIED MARK ON NON-ACCRUALS' FIGURE IN THIS RECORD. *** The cohort ladder I built and used all session — TCPC 19.4c / OTF 22.8c / OBDC 29.5c / PNNT 31.1c / FSK 47.9c / WHF 50.4c / MFIC 55.1c — DOES NOT MEASURE MARKING DISCIPLINE. Implied mark = non-accrual FV% / cost% is dominated by CONCENTRATION AND TIMING: it tells you WHEN a manager's worst credit blew up, not how honestly it marks. Proof: 79% of OBDC's entire Q2 unrealized loss is ONE second lien (Loparex, $130.6M marked 63c -> 5c, independently confirmed via PitchBook). Ex-that-single-name OBDC computes at 38.7c rather than 29.5c. A manager whose big blow-up is RECENT looks harsh; one whose blow-up was years ago and is already written to zero looks soft — with identical discipline. THE LADDER MUST BE RECOMPUTED EX-LARGEST-NAME BEFORE IT IS EVER USED TO ORDER MANAGERS AGAIN, and until then no verdict may rest on it. Note the ordering may survive — ex-Loparex OBDC still marks harsher than FSK, WHF and MFIC as published — but that is unproven for the others because only OBDC has been decomposed. Affected: every classification below that cites the ladder, and the court contexts for MFIC, OTF and OBDC.
